title: The Barber's Tale of his Fifth Brother
summary: The barber then laughed merrily as he remembered his fifth brother, Al-Nashshar, whose name became a proverb across the East:
keywords: the barber's tale of his fifth brother
full_text:
The barber then laughed merrily as he remembered his fifth brother, Al-Nashshar, whose name became a proverb across the East:

"My brother Al-Nashshar was a lazy fellow who inherited one hundred silver dirhams upon our father’s death. Instead of investing in steady trade, he spent the entire sum purchasing a large wicker basket filled with fragile glassware—crystal bottles, cut-glass bowls, and delicate perfume flasks. He set his basket against a sunny wall in the market square, rested his back against the bricks, folded his arms, and began to weave magnificent daydreams.

'With these hundred dirhams of glassware,' he murmured to himself, 'I shall make two hundred dirhams in profit. With those two hundred, I shall buy fine Syrian pottery and double my money to four hundred. Within two years, I shall amass ten thousand dirhams and buy a magnificent shop in the jewelers' bazaar. I shall trade in pearls, diamonds, and rubies until I am worth a hundred thousand dinars!

Then,' he whispered, closing his eyes in ecstasy, 'I shall demand the hand of the Grand Vizier’s daughter in marriage. On our wedding night, when she enters my chamber adorned in jewels and bows humbly to offer me a cup of spiced wine, I shall pretend to be proud and haughty. I shall turn my face away to test her submissiveness. And when she kneels and begs for my regard, I shall draw back my foot and kick her thus, to teach her who is master!'

Lost in his grandiose illusion, Al-Nashshar lashed out with his right foot in earnest! His heavy leather boot struck the wicker basket squarely in the center. The basket flipped into the street, crashing against the cobblestones with a deafening shatter. Crystal, colored glass, and perfume bottles were pulverized into a thousand worthless shards!

Al-Nashshar opened his eyes and saw his entire fortune lying in glittering dust at his feet. He tore his hair, beat his breast, and wept bitter tears while the entire bazaar erupted in uncontrollable laughter. He had destroyed his reality in the pursuit of an arrogant shadow."
moral: Daydreaming of haughty triumph without laying the foundation of labor shatters one's hopes into dust.
